meta.access_note: All figures read from search-engine extracts; direct fetches were blocked. No value is high confidence. 'judgment' marks modeling choices.
meta.life_definition: lifeReactive = expected service life with reactive (leak-driven) repairs only; maintained life = lifeReactive + lifeAddedPlanned. Lender EULs (ASTM E2018) assume routine maintenance and are treated as approximately the maintained life.

tpo.note: EUL 20 treated as maintained life. NRCA 15-35 by grade. UFC 3-110-03 Ch.1 limits TPO to roofs with an anticipated life of 10 yrs or less.

coating_restoration.note: Life of a coating restoration before a recoat or replacement is needed. A recoat on a dry substrate adds 10-15 yrs and is modeled as a separate event. No ASTM, NRCA or RCMA standard maps mils to years.

marketLifeAdjustPct._note: Percent change to the national baseline life. All values are judgment, low confidence. Reasoning: Nearmap 2026 shows ~19-23% shorter cycles in hot-humid and high temperature-swing counties (upper bound); Texas hail is FEMA NRI Very High; Arrhenius heat aging affects TPO and bitumen; Galvalume marine-air life is about -20%; mid-Atlantic freeze-thaw affects bitumen and coatings.

repairCurve.form: repairPctOfReplacement(x) = base + peakAdd * x^beta, where x = age / expectedLife (capped at xCap)
repairCurve.plannedMaintenanceEffect: lengthens expectedLife, which lowers x at each age
repairCurve.note: Right half-bathtub: early defects are absorbed by warranties. The cubic exponent is a judgment (a typical Weibull wear-out beta); the CERL coefficients were not obtained. The ~1%/yr mean matches the JM 1-3% figure and the $0.09-0.19/sf survey range at $12-15/sf replacement.

typeNotes._note: repairBurdenMult scales the repair-curve level; lifeAdjustPct is applied in addition to the market adjustment. All values are judgment, low confidence, based on ~70-80% of leaks occurring at flashings and penetrations (Roofing Contractor) and USACE's observation that rooftop equipment drives flashing complexity and roof traffic.

industrial.note: Few penetrations and little traffic. CBECS: metal dominant (662k of warehouse buildings), then synthetic/rubber (131k), then built-up (59k).

office.note: More RTUs and penetrations; HVAC technician traffic. CBECS: synthetic/rubber 180k, built-up 160k, metal 207k (much of it steep-slope).

retail.note: Moderate RTU density; tenant signage and food-tenant exhaust penetrations. CBECS mercantile: synthetic/rubber 136k, metal 135k.

multifamily.note: Many condensers and vents per sq ft; amenity traffic on podium roofs. Not covered by CBECS. Garden-style steep-slope roofs are out of scope.

mixed.note: Residential penetration density plus retail exhausts; amenity decks.

medical.note: Densest heavy equipment and technician traffic. Healthcare all-systems maintenance runs $4.50-10/sf vs office $1.60-3.20 (single vendor source).

k12.note: GAO-20-494: about 28,000 schools need roofing updates; districts patch to defer replacement. NCES 2012-13: roofs fair/poor in about 25% of permanent buildings and 42% of portables. Deferral belongs in the maintenance-regime input.

commonness._note: Judgment flags from CBECS 2018 Table B11 (warehouse, office, mercantile, education; synthetic/rubber is not split into TPO/EPDM; no mod-bit category; metal includes steep-slope) and property-types.md section 4 (medical, multifamily, mixed).

endOfLife.rule: First replacement may be a recover if the roof is dry (wet area under ~25%) and has one existing covering; the next replacement must be a tear-off.
